questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code keeps a slow audit sink from overwhelming the service? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The audit sink stalls and the deepest lane reaches 300 queued events. What does the consumer do next?
choices: Stops calling poll until the lanes drain, to avoid fetching more records
Pauses its assigned partitions but keeps calling poll, which returns no records while paused
Blocks inside dispatch until the lane queue has room again
Drops new records for the slow lane and commits their offsets

questions.prompt: Why are the offsets recorded with completed.merge(tp, offset + 1, Math::max) safe to commit?
choices: Because commitSync sorts offsets before sending them to the broker
Because each partition always maps to the same single-threaded lane, so its records finish in order and the highest completed offset implies all earlier ones are done
Because the sink writes are transactional, so earlier offsets are never lost
Because ConcurrentHashMap guarantees work is executed in submission order

questions.prompt: What can happen to events if the process is killed right after the sink wrote an event but before commitCompleted ran?
choices: The event is lost, because its offset was committed before processing
The event is redelivered after restart and may be written to the sink a second time
The event is moved to a dead letter topic automatically
The consumer refuses to restart until the offset is repaired manually
